source.title: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms.
source.location: Results section 2.1 text (water control condition; Figure S1A cited but supplement not on disk)

injury: transverse amputations posterior to the pharynx and anterior to the tail

intervention.description: Pre-tail fragments were amputated and left to regenerate in plain water with no drug added.

readout.method: visual head-shape classification against species-specific head shapes, with geometric morphometrics

notes: Text states that regeneration in water has 100% fidelity to the species-specific head shape and that variant species-specific head shapes were never seen in this condition (cites Figure S1A, which is not on disk). No n is stated for this arm, so the percentage is entered as the count and n_total is null. Pass A instead used the Figure 2A morphometric group size (n=8) as the count; that group is a morphometric subsample, not the scored control cohort, so the text percentage is used here.

adjudication.note: B's text-based 100% control row kept; A's row used a morphometric subsample n as if it were the scored cohort
